title.sub: Chapter 1: Night Rain at Pine Ferry. Whatever you choose, someone else inherits it.
duel.instruction: Chain three forms, each flowing into the next.
duel.rule: Soft gives way to hard. Hard lifts into the step. The step hides the stillness. Stillness softens again.
duel.no_form: No form took shape. You survive on instinct alone.
scroll.mark.wound: A scar on your sword arm that still runs cold.
ch1.ferry.p1: Rain hammers the roof of the Pine Ferry inn. You are Yan Ruo, an outer disciple of the Tingyu Pavilion, and a sealed jade slip rests against your ribs. Your master pressed it into your hands with one instruction: the Iron Crane Sect, by dawn, unread.
ch1.ferry.p2: Across the room, a ragged old man has been watching your wine jar for a long time. The lamp throws every shadow toward the door. His falls the other way.
ch1.bandits.beggar_friend: The old man drains the cup and sighs. “Kind hands are rarer than good swords. Keep your lamp lit, little cultivator.” Then he is simply in the corner, though you never saw him stand.
ch1.bandits.beggar_cold: The old man shrugs and turns back to the rain. The cup you did not pour frosts over on the table.
ch1.bandits.beggar_tested: The old man grins with too many teeth. “Something that remembers,” he says, and says nothing more.
ch1.bandits.p2: Every lamp in the inn gutters at once. The door blows inward, and three cultivators in black willow-bark robes walk in on the cold. Dark mist coils from their blades: resentful energy, the crooked path. The one with the scarred jaw is Gu Tie of the Black Willow.
ch1.bandits.p3: “The jade slip,” he says. “Set it on the table, and you keep your golden core.”
ch1.bandits.c_decoy: Slide a forged slip across the table.
ch1.duel.intro_sword: Your blade leaves its sheath with a sound like a struck bell. Gu Tie smiles, and the dark mist on his sabre rises to meet it.
ch1.duel.intro_silver: Gu Tie crushes the spirit stones in his fist and lets the dust fall. “Wrong answer.”
ch1.duel.intro_decoy: Gu Tie presses his thumb to the forged slip and feels nothing inside. His smile dies. The first cut comes before the jade hits the floor.
ch1.after.links_2: Your chain never breaks. Gu Tie’s sabre spins away across the floor, the dark mist bleeding out of it, and he drops to one knee, unmarked but beaten.
ch1.after.links_1: It was not clean. His last cut opens your sleeve and cold resentment seeps into the wound, but your blade finds him first.
ch1.after.links_0: You lose the rhythm entirely and win on stubbornness and raw spiritual power. Gu Tie falls; your meridians ache like bruises.
ch1.after.p2: His disciples have fled into the rain. He slumps against the cold stove, the black mist thinning around him. Behind you, the old man’s shadow has stopped moving.
ch1.after.c_spare: Spare him. Help him to his feet.
ch1.after.c_kill: End it. He would not have spared you.
ch1.after.c_token: Take his ghost-binding token and leave him.
ch1.letter.p1: Dawn. The rain has thinned to mist over the river, and the mountains above Pine Ferry float on it like ink on wet paper. The seal on the jade slip cracked in the fight: only a hairline, but enough to let your spiritual sense slip inside.
ch1.letter.c_burn: Burn it with a talisman. Some secrets should die.
ch1.scroll.intro: The ferry bell rings. Before you leave, you write down everything you are leaving behind and seal it with a drop of your blood. The next one to walk this road will find it.
ch1.debt.spared: Gu Tie owes you his life, and he knows it.
ch1.debt.killed: Gu Tie’s sworn brothers want your blood, and the crooked path has a long memory.
ch1.debt.token: You carry Gu Tie’s ghost-binding token. The Black Willow wants it back, and so does whatever it binds.
ch1.secret.read: You read the slip. It names the Iron Crane Sect’s master as a traitor who trades in stolen golden cores.
ch1.secret.sealed: You delivered the slip unread. The Iron Crane Sect owes you a favor.
ch1.secret.burned: The slip is ash. Someone will come asking what it said.
ch1.witness.friend: The old man at Pine Ferry, if he is a man, remembers your cup of wine.
ch1.witness.cold: The old man at Pine Ferry, if he is a man, saw you turn away.
ch1.witness.tested: The old man at Pine Ferry, if he is a man, remembers your question. He has not forgotten your face.
ch1.epilogue.heading: The Inheritor
ch1.epilogue.p1: Years later. You are Shen Mo, a ferryman’s apprentice at Pine Ferry with no spiritual roots worth mentioning. A scroll surfaces in the river reeds, sealed with a drop of old blood. You unroll it and read about a cultivator who stood where you now stand.
ch1.epilogue.gu_spared: A man with a scarred jaw waits on your dock, no dark mist about him now. He says he owes a debt to the one who wrote this, and he wants to know where she went.
ch1.epilogue.gu_killed: Two men with Gu Tie’s scarred jaw watch your ferry from the far bank, black mist pooling at their feet. His sworn brothers have not stopped looking.
ch1.epilogue.gu_token: A black jade token hangs from your ferry post, cold even at noon. Someone left it there. Something will come back for it.
ch1.epilogue.technique: The scroll also teaches you the first form of {technique_short}. You can trace it with a ferry pole, but you have not earned it.
ch1.epilogue.unbuilt: Chapter 2 is not built yet. This is where Shen Mo’s choices would begin, shaped by everything Yan Ruo left behind.
